title: My Grad School Mentor
content: Gene Halvorsen was my dissertation advisor at Michigan. Brilliant guy, kind of gruff, always had chalk on his sleeves. But what made Gene special wasn't just his intellect. He cared about real-world impact. We'd have these long debates about taxes and fund returns, and he'd always push me: 'What does this mean for the person at the kitchen table?' My dissertation ended up being about how much of a fund's return quietly disappears to taxes before an investor ever sees it. The answer was a lot more than people assumed. That number shocked people. It's basically what I've been chasing ever since.
follow_up: Gene taught me something I still carry: the best research answers questions real people have. Not abstract puzzles - real problems. Every time I write something now, I ask myself: would this help someone at their kitchen table? That's Gene's voice in my head.
